field.name: content
field.p: (From Google Groups, originally posted by KI6UGB on January 26, 2014)

For those that are interested. On Thursday Jan 16 at 7:30PM I will attempt to tie our IRLP node to a net in Southern California, An outdoor adventure and ham club called OAUSA puts on weekly nets on a variety of different outdoor subjects. This week's net is on APRS.
I say "attempt" as the last time I tried I could hear them but they could not hear me to check in.

It's a good group. I met up with them on a ten day 4x4 trip through Arizona, New Mexico and Utah a few years back. We used Simplex APRS (no digipeaters in the back country) to keep track of where all our vehicles were. One of the guys used a pactor-3 modem with his HF rig to send photos back to his family.

The net starts at 7:30 with a rather lengthy check-in procedure and typically runs to 9:00 PM. The net is held on the Western Reflector at Node 9251. For more information visit the OAUSA website at forums.oausa.net.
If you have time, give a listen and check-in. Hope you enjoy.

field.name: content
field.p: (Originally posted by KI6UGB on February 4, 2014)
Hi all, a couple of updates regarding the transition to the new website:

- 25 people have created accounts so far. Thanks! There are a couple of accounts I was unable to verify as no callsign was provided and I couldn't find the email address in the database. Those users have been notified, and unless I hear back with a callsign in the next week or so, those accounts will be deleted.
- For those who tried to renew their membership with PayPal only to find it didn't work, worry not, the Store page has been fixed, and PayPal works again.

- I highly encourage everyone to subscribe to any or all of our three forums. From any forum's page, click the "Subscribe" button at the top (be sure you're logged in) to receive an email whenever a new topic is posted. Charlie and I hope to slowly move from the Google Group to the forums.

- Any club officials or committee chairs who need to be able to edit certain pages will need to request access from me. John WB6FRZ kindly volunteered to test this system, and I believe we got the issues ironed out. Officials will be able to edit only their specific page, and that page will only be editable by the appropriate official.
If there are any questions, issues, or comments that arise, please don't hesitate to contact me. Thanks for your patience as we go through this transition!
-Sutter KI6ZON, SCRA Webmaster

field.name: content
field.p: (Originally posted by Lewis, KK6BK on February 18, 2014)

When you subscribe to the forums, is it possible to request a digest like some other discussion boards do? That combines all submissions into a digest for all those submitted in one day or one week, whichever you select. It's not an issue at this point, but when discussion boards become busy it prevents filling your mailbox with email for each individual update to the forum.

field.name: content
field.p: (Originally posted by KI6UGB on February 18, 2014)

Hi Lewis, when you subscribe to a whole forum (Activities, Public Service, etc.), you will receive an email for each new topic, but not for replies to topics. You must subscribe to topics individually to get emails for each new message. Hopefully this will keep the email volume down. -Sutter

field.p: (Originally posted by NH7X on March 20, 2014)
Tonight (3/20/14) at 7:30PM the UHF repeater will be linked to the OAUSA net via IRLP. Tonight's topic: Ham Mobile Radio Install.

Discussion will focus on a good, clean, neat installation of your mobile radio to ensure years of noise-free operation. Participants are invited to share best practices, tips, techniques, and clever solutions regarding mobile radio installations, as every vehicle presents unique challenges for antenna placement, power pickup, and radio setup.
The net organizers welcome topic suggestions for future sessions.

record.field: Michael Von der Porten's email has been hijacked

field.name: content
field.p: (Originally posted by WB6JAO and KG6GEX on September 15, 2014)
A security alert warns that Michael Von der Porten's AOL email account (mikevdpca@aim.com) has been compromised. Fraudulent messages requesting money are being sent from this address.
Please disregard such messages and mark them as spam or phishing. Bill Finkelstein said he would contact Michael by phone to let him know of the breach.
Bill also recommends that anyone still relying on AOL or Yahoo email accounts consider migrating to Gmail for better security protections.
